sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:132389
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 28804 of 2024

Applicant :- Mamta
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Phool Singh Yadav,Vaibhav Yadav
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed today on behalf of the applicant is taken on record.
2. Sri Phool Singh Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Manoj Kumar Singh, learned brief holder for the State-respondent.

3. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
536 of 2022, under Sections 420, 467,468, 471, 120-B IPC, Police Station- Bhognipur, District- Kanpur Dehat, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

4. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and one another by her father-in-law through an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. and as per allegation, when informant was in jail in connection with some other case then behind him, applicant, who is his daughter-in-law, with the help of her husband prepared a fake consent letter of the informant and got benefit from the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana.

Mamta vs State Of U.P. on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58444419/
1

5. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that entire allegations levelled against the applicant and her husband is totally false and actually in the year 2015, a FIR of rape was lodged by the applicant against her father-in-law i.e. informant of the case and in that case, he was convicted during trial and during pendency of the appeal when he was released on bail then after release, he prepared a fabricated and fake document dated 17.02.2021, which was his consent letter and on the basis of this fake and fabricated document, he lodged the FIR of the present case.
6. He further submitted that even the alleged consent letter was not required for the purpose to get benefit of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana.
7.
He further submitted that applicant is not an absconder and the charge sheet of the present case was filed in the year 2024.

8. He further submitted that applicant is a lady and all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate-I Class and applicant is not having any previous criminal history and she is in jail in the present matter since 09.07.2024.
9. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
10. I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. However, as per allegation,while informant, who is father-in-law of the applicant, was in jail,
applicant along with her husband on the basis of his fake consent letter got the benefit of Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana but it reflects that in the year 2015, applicant lodged a FIR of rape against her father-in-law i.e. informant of the case and in that case, he was convicted and after released on bail during pendency of his appeal, FIR of the present case was lodged by him, therefore, the argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that after released on bail, a fake and fabricated document was prepared by the informant, who is highly inimical with the applicant and her husband and on the basis of which, FIR of the present case was lodged, cannot be completely ruled out at this stage.

12. Further, however, FIR of the present case was lodged in the year in December 2022 and applicant is in jail since 09.07.2024 but it reflects that even investigation of the case could only be concluded in the year 2024 and therefore, the submission advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is not an offender, cannot be completely ruled out.

13. Further, applicant is a lady and all the alleged offences are tribal by Magistrate-I Class and she is not having any previous criminal history and she is in jail in the present matter since 09.07.2024.
14. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Mamta vs State Of U.P. on 14 August, 2024

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58444419/
2 15.
Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

16. Let the applicant- Mamta be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
17. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

18. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

Order Date :- 14.8.2024 KK Patel  Mamta vs State Of U.P. on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58444419/
